title: ANDY — Queer Communities Across Time
intro: A journey into queer history and the Silver Factory community, bringing lecture, drag, karaoke, anecdotes and dance into a theatre performance.
text: Andy Warhol is the starting point for an encounter with queer lives across time. Research, imagination and autobiography bring life in twentieth-century New York into conversation with queer experience today.

The project developed through three iterations: a university seminar lecture at Freie Universität Berlin; a lecture performance and artist talk at Literarischer Salon Berlin Friedrichshain; and theatre performances at Ost Passage Theater Leipzig.
facts: Alex Jarewski, Ocean X, guest Noah Jason
credits: Costume: G3, Lars Schleifer, Gallanegra Upcycling, Victoria Vau, Aylin. Technical team: Vrena Zucker, Max Latinski. Photography credits were not supplied.

title: Time Smuggler
intro: The body as architecture. A collaborative performance exploring how bodies in relation transform our experience of space and time.
text: Initiated by Isabel Lewis and developed with artists from the Class for Performative Arts at the Academy of Fine Arts Leipzig, Time Smuggler creates temporary architectures within existing architecture. Bodies, movement, gestures and voices extend spatial structures and create shifting compositions.
Dreaming and dérive inform the approach. Drawing on Alina Popa’s Imitation of Dream and Guy Debord’s Theory of the Dérive, the ensemble shifts habitual patterns of movement and perception.
An evolving vocabulary of scores provides starting points for improvisation. Each iteration responds to the architecture, rhythms and social conditions of its surroundings.
facts: Artists from the Class for Performative Arts, Academy of Fine Arts Leipzig
Leipzig academy students and local participants
credits: Venice photographs: Enrico Fiorese (files beginning _E1 and _R9A); Haiguang Li (TSphoto files). Other image credits were not supplied.
editions: Galerie für Zeitgenössische Kunst, Leipzig — adapted for The Word for Museum is Forest
Ocean Space and public space, Venice — October 2024
quote: TIME SMUGGLER proposed a collective art-making process, one that incorporates individual positions in ways that empower their voices and textures, rather than compromising them.
Eleni Michaelidi · curator and art historian · curatorial statement, December 2023

title: A.PHANTASIA — Fields of Imagining
intro: Computer-generated and code-manipulated images of phosphenes and inner, usually unseen experiences.
text: Glowing fields probe the boundaries between sensory perception, mental imagery and imagination. The images belong to a larger body of artistic research connecting cognitive, somatic and philosophical approaches to experience.

Phosphenes are impressions of light in the absence of external light. The project gives form to subjective experiences that are not ordinarily visible to others, inviting viewers to reflect on their own sensory and imaginative worlds.
The works use imagination as a bridge between different experiences of perception. This gallery presents the supplied still images; it does not imply completed animations.
facts: Computer-generated and code-manipulated imagery / digital prints

title: PHANTASMAGORIA — Kartographische Morphismen
intro: Cartographic material becomes abstract form: a way of travelling through places, news, memory and feeling.
text: Places and coordinates become symbols for experiences, stories and events that leave a deep impression. Abstract two-dimensional objects made from cartographic material respond to places that briefly enter the centre of attention before disappearing into the periphery.
The works record journeys that are mental and emotional rather than physical. Maps, a portal to imagination and learning since childhood, form the visual starting point.
The process began during the Covid-19 lockdowns and continues as an ongoing practice of reflection and processing.
facts: Kolkata · DRC · Kolkata Cloudburst · Marshall Islands
credits: Artworks: Oyu Ocean. Labels below follow the supplied filenames.

title: (Embodied) tools for decentralization
intro: A sound tool turns the performers’ movements into a shared exploration of bodily, social and spatial orientation.
text: Integrated into costume sleeves, mobile devices produce melodic digital sounds. Movement modulates the sounds in real time; the performers respond to the evolving soundscape in a situation of mutual affectivity.

The sound-generator prototype uses sensors in conventional smartphones and was developed with artist and computer scientist Jonathan Schneider. The performance draws on decentralised movement patterns of migratory birds and schools of fish.
Presented within FABULATIVE LORE: Tools and Handiness, the work explores how objects carry stories, scores and possibilities for interaction.
facts: FABULATIVE LORE: Tools and Handiness, with Eszter Szöke
credits: Photography: Laura Wichmann. Sound-tool development: Jonathan Schneider in collaboration with Lissy Willberg.

title: LNX
intro: A performance in a prologue and three stages, structured through four distinct lighting modes.
text: The supplied notes identify LNX as an acronym for Lil Nas X and give the work’s earlier title as Closing {Panorama}.
The lighting sequence moves from a prologue with warm light and a static searchlight through green, blue and white flood light. These modes give the performance its changing visual conditions.

title: POOLBOY
intro: A celebration of queer joy, connection and playfulness, set against the backdrop of a shimmering blue pool.
text: Laughter, swimming and shared moments bring diverse identities together. Water becomes a metaphor for fluidity: a space where boundaries dissolve and individual stories interweave.
Shot on a handheld camera phone, the film was filmed, edited and first screened during an artist residency in the German countryside.
